description: The plot illustrates how two metrics—model perplexity and GPU memory ratio—vary as the “Recent Sequence Ratio (%)” changes, with both metrics shown on shared x-values but different y-axes. The x-axis is labeled “Recent Sequence Ratio (%)” on a linear scale, spanning roughly 10% to 100% with labeled ticks at 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100. The left y-axis is labeled “Perplexity,” linear from about 4.2 to 4.7 with ticks at 0.1 increments, and includes a red dashed horizontal reference line labeled “Full Cache PPL” at approximately 4.38. The right y-axis is labeled “GPU Mem. Ratio (%)” on a linear scale from about 40% to 100% with ticks every 10%, and includes a blue dashed horizontal reference line labeled “Full Cache GPU Mem.” at 100%. The perplexity series is an orange solid line with circular markers: it starts near 4.59 at ~10%, decreases through ~4.45 (20%), ~4.39 (30%) to a low around 4.30 at ~40%, then rises slightly to ~4.33–4.34 around 50–60%, dips to ~4.29 at ~70%, increases to ~4.34 at ~80%, and ends around ~4.39 at ~90% and ~4.38 at ~100%. The GPU memory ratio series is a blue solid line with circular markers: it begins near ~41% at ~10% recent sequence ratio, increases gradually to about ~42% (20%), ~43% (30%), ~44% (40%), ~45% (50%), ~46% (60%), and ~48% (70%), then rises to roughly ~55% at ~80%, jumps sharply to about ~98% at ~90%, and finishes near ~99–100% at ~100%.
